title: Bone development in patients with spinal muscular atrophy (SMA)
summary:
Spinal muscular atrophy (SMA) is a genetic disorder. A mutation in the SMN1 gene leads to muscle wasting, scoliosis, and other symptoms. In adolescence, we perform spinal fusion surgery on many SMA patients to correct scoliosis.
In this study, we aim to investigate the impact of the mutation on bone and cartilage. To do this, we are examining bone and cartilage fragments that are collected during surgery and would otherwise be discarded, as well as blood samples, X-ray, MRI, and CT images (which are routinely obtained for the surgery). The same examinations are being conducted on patients without SMA who come to us for spinal fusion surgery.
conditions: Infantile spinal muscular atrophy, type I [Werdnig-Hoffman]

From patients without SMA who undergo spinal fusion surgery, bone and cartilage material, as well as blood, urine, and sputum samples, will be analyzed, and patient data and clinical X-ray, MRI, and CT images (which are routinely obtained for the surgeries) will be evaluated.

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
Following appropriate counseling and informed consent, the study will include all children and adolescents between the ages of 5 and 17 with a spinal deformity and SMA or another underlying condition who are undergoing surgical correction in the Department of Pediatric Orthopedics at UMG.
Exclusion criteria:
Patients who do not meet the criteria listed above or who do not consent to participate in the study are excluded.
